facts.fact: Vanguard reports that the NIMC's NIN verification portal is in use by banks and mobile operators for real-time identity checks, and was disrupted in early July 2025 during a switch to a new platform.

Vanguard reports that banks, mobile network operators and the Nigerian Immigration Service all rely on NIMC's NIN verification platform, and that NIMC also urged an alternative tokenisation method that verifies identity without exposing the NIN.

NGA.note: Nothing on the civil register stated.

NIMC changed its software vendor to Bluesalt for verification; who operates, maintains or owns the ID system is not stated.
No public register keyed on the NIN stated.

facts.fact: Vanguard reports that banks and mobile operators link customers to their NIN records through NIMC's verification platform, which was in use until its July 2025 disruption.
Vanguard reports that banks and mobile network operators verify customers' NINs through NIMC's platform to open accounts and register SIM cards.
Vanguard reports that NIN verification is relied on by banks, mobile network operators (SIM registration, replacement and number portability) and the Immigration Service for passport processing.
